shortcuts.rule: a file with no "Feature:" line is invalid and fails with a ParseError
shortcuts.input: "# just a comment\n" (or an empty string)
shortcuts.what: returns null (via `feature!`) instead of throwing a ParseError; the result is not a Feature at all

shortcuts.rule: step text is the text after the keyword and one space
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: X
 Scenario: A
  Given a step   
"
shortcuts.what: trims trailing whitespace from the text with trimEnd(), returning "a step" instead of "a step   "

shortcuts.rule: doc string lines have the indentation of the opening quotes removed
shortcuts.input: a doc string whose opening quotes are indented 6 spaces and holding the line "  ab" (indented 2)
shortcuts.what: slices every line at the column of the opening quotes, so it cuts into the text and returns "" instead of only removing the indentation ("ab")

shortcuts.rule: a line inside a scenario that is none of the recognised forms fails at that line with a ParseError
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: X
  Scenario: S
    | a | b |
" (a table row with no step before it in the scenario)
shortcuts.what: dereferences steps[-1] and throws a TypeError ("Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'table')") instead of a ParseError with line 3

shortcuts.rule: a line inside a scenario that is none of the recognised forms fails at that line with a ParseError
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: X
  Scenario: S
    """
    x
    """
" (a doc string with no step before it)
shortcuts.what: throws a TypeError ("Cannot set properties of undefined (setting 'docString')") instead of a ParseError naming line 3

shortcuts.rule: lines between "Feature:" and the first Background:/Scenario:/tag line are the feature's description and are skipped
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: X
  | some description |
  Scenario: S
    Given a
"
shortcuts.what: treats the description line as a table row for a non-existent step and crashes with a TypeError (steps is null) instead of skipping it

shortcuts.rule: doc string lines have the indentation of the opening quotes removed
shortcuts.input: a step followed by a doc string whose opening quotes are indented 6 spaces and a content line "    abc" indented only 4
shortcuts.what: slices a fixed 6 characters off every line regardless of whether they are whitespace, returning "c" and losing the text "ab"

shortcuts.rule: doc strings and tables belong to the step before them; an invalid line inside a scenario fails with a ParseError naming its line
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: F
  Scenario: S
    | a | b |
" (or a """ doc string directly after "Scenario:" or "Background:", with no step before it)
shortcuts.what: reads steps[steps.length - 1] as undefined and crashes with a TypeError when it sets .table or .docString on it, instead of throwing a ParseError at line 3

shortcuts.rule: a second "Feature:" line fails at that line
shortcuts.input: "Feature:\nFeature: Again"
shortcuts.what: an empty feature name is treated as 'no feature yet', so no error is thrown; it returns a feature named "Again"

shortcuts.rule: the file must start with a "Feature:" line; the error is only for content before any Feature line
shortcuts.input: "Feature:\n  Scenario: a\n    Given x"
shortcuts.what: throws 'expected Feature at line 2' even though line 1 is a Feature line, because the empty name counts as no feature

shortcuts.rule: a line inside a scenario that is none of the valid forms fails at that line with a ParseError
shortcuts.input: "Feature: X\n  Scenario: a\n    | a |" (a table, or a doc string, with no step before it)
shortcuts.what: throws a TypeError (no previous step to attach to) instead of a ParseError with a line property

shortcuts.rule: doc string lines have the indentation of the opening quotes removed
shortcuts.input:
Feature: F
  Scenario: S
    Given a doc
      """
      {
    }
      """
shortcuts.what: it cuts a fixed number of characters (the opening quotes' column) off every line instead of removing only the leading indentation, so a line indented less than the quotes loses its real text: the line "    }" becomes "" instead of "}" (docString is ["{", ""])

shortcuts.rule: a table or doc string belongs to the step before it; any other line inside a scenario fails at that line
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: A
  Scenario: One
    Given x
  Scenario: Two
    | a | b |
    Given y"
shortcuts.what: `last` is never reset when a new Scenario:/Background: starts, so the table row right after "Scenario: Two" (no step before it in that scenario) is silently attached to scenario One's step "Given x" instead of raising a ParseError at line 5; the same happens to a """ doc string placed there

shortcuts.rule: a line starting with "#" is a comment and is skipped
shortcuts.input: "# a comment\nFeature: A"
shortcuts.what: the comment check runs only after a Feature: line has been seen, so a leading comment is treated as content before Feature: and throws ParseError at line 1 instead of being skipped

shortcuts.rule: a step's text is what follows the keyword and one space
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: A
  Scenario: One
    Given 
" (also "    Given a step  ")
shortcuts.what: every line is trimmed before matching, so "Given " no longer matches the step pattern and throws ParseError at line 3 instead of giving a step with text ""; trailing spaces in step text are also lost

shortcuts.rule: doc string lines have the opening quotes' indentation removed
shortcuts.input:
Feature: F
  Scenario: S
    Given a doc
      """
    less indented
      """
shortcuts.what: it cuts a fixed number of characters (the column of the opening quotes) off every line with lines[j].slice(ind). On the content line that removes the 4 spaces and also the first 2 letters, so the doc string is ["ss indented"] when it should be ["less indented"]. Text is lost, not just indentation.

shortcuts.rule: lines starting with "#" are comments and are skipped everywhere
shortcuts.input:
"# leading comment
Feature: Payouts
  Scenario: One
    Given a step"
shortcuts.what: The first non-blank line must start with "Feature:" before comments are checked, so the comment on line 1 throws ParseError at line 1 when it should be skipped and the file should parse.

shortcuts.rule: doc string lines have the opening quotes' indentation removed
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: F
  Scenario: S
    Given a doc
      """
    abcdef
      """"
shortcuts.what: It cuts a fixed number of characters (the opening quotes' column) from every line without checking that they are whitespace. The less-indented line "    abcdef" comes out as "ef" and loses real content.

shortcuts.rule: doc string lines are kept as written, apart from the indentation
shortcuts.input:
"Feature: F
  Scenario: S
    Given a doc
    """
    a  
    """"
shortcuts.what: It calls trimEnd on every doc string line, so the line "a  " is returned as "a".

shortcuts.rule: a step's text is what follows the keyword and one space
shortcuts.input: "Feature: F\n  Scenario: S\n    Given a step   "
shortcuts.what: It calls trimEnd on the step text, returning "a step" when the text after the keyword and one space is "a step   ".

shortcuts.rule: each error is a ParseError with a line; doc strings and tables belong to the step before them
shortcuts.input: "Feature: F\n  Scenario: S\n    | a | b |" (or a doc string straight after "Scenario:" or "Background:")
shortcuts.what: There is no step before the table or doc string, so `last` is null and the code throws a TypeError instead of a ParseError naming the line.

shortcuts.rule: a line starting with "#" is a comment and is skipped; only other content before "Feature:" is an error
shortcuts.input:
"# payouts suite
Feature: Payouts
  Scenario: One
    Given a step
"
shortcuts.what: the no-Feature check runs before comments are skipped, so the comment on line 1 throws ParseError "unexpected line at line 1" instead of the file parsing as feature "Payouts" with one scenario

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content (context, removed, added lines) is mapped word by word through identifier entries
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; inside a hunk, a removed line whose content is "-- a/docs/Sheet.md" (so the diff line is "--- a/docs/Sheet.md"), or an added line with content "++ b/docs/Sheet.md" (diff line "+++ b/docs/Sheet.md")
shortcuts.what: There is no diff parsing, so any line starting with "--- a/" or "+++ b/" is treated as a file header no matter where it appears. The hunk line gets path-mapped instead of identifier-mapped: "Sheet" is not replaced, and "docs/Sheet.md" is wrongly added to unmapped. Where a path entry does cover it, the line gets path-rewritten instead.

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content (removed/added/context lines) is mapped word by word
shortcuts.input: identifier Sheet->Invoice, path ledger->billing; a hunk '@@ -1 +1 @@' whose removed line has content '-- a/Sheet' (so the diff line is '--- a/Sheet'), then '+x'
shortcuts.what: Lines are classified by regex alone without tracking hunk structure, so the removed line is treated as a '--- a/' file header: 'Sheet' is not mapped to 'Invoice' and 'Sheet' is wrongly reported as an unmapped path

shortcuts.rule: Only hunk content is identifier-mapped; '\ No newline at end of file' markers and other non-hunk lines are kept byte for byte
shortcuts.input: identifier entry real 'blob' public 'file'; a diff containing the marker '\ No newline at end of file' (or 'new file mode 100644')
shortcuts.what: Identifiers are replaced on every non-header line, producing '\ No newline at end of blob' (and 'new blob mode 100644')

shortcuts.rule: Public paths in header lines are mapped (and unmapped ones reported) as whole paths
shortcuts.input: path entry real 'billing/my invoice.ts' public 'ledger/my sheet.ts' and a header '--- a/ledger/my sheet.ts'; or an unmapped header '+++ b/docs/my notes.md'
shortcuts.what: Paths are captured with \S+ so they stop at the first space: 'ledger/my sheet.ts' becomes 'billing/my sheet.ts' via the directory entry instead of 'billing/my invoice.ts', and 'docs/my' is reported as unmapped instead of 'docs/my notes.md'

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content (removed/added lines) is mapped word by word
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; inside a hunk, a removed line whose text is "-- Sheet note" (diff line "--- Sheet note") or an added line "++ Sheet" (diff line "+++ Sheet")
shortcuts.what: There is no hunk tracking, so any line starting with "--- " or "+++ " is treated as a file header. "Sheet" is not replaced with "Invoice", and "Sheet note" is wrongly reported as an unmapped path.

shortcuts.rule: Paths in diff --git header lines are mapped (and unmapped ones reported)
shortcuts.input: Path entry real "billing" public "ledger"; header "diff --git a/ledger/my file.ts b/ledger/my file.ts" (a path containing a space), or a quoted path
shortcuts.what: The regex only accepts space-free, unquoted paths. The line falls through to identifier replacement, "ledger" stays unmapped in the header, and nothing is reported as unmapped.

shortcuts.rule: File paths in ---/+++ headers are mapped
shortcuts.input: Path entry real "billing/invoice.ts" public "ledger/sheet.ts"; header "--- a/ledger/sheet.ts\t2024-01-01 00:00:00" (unified-diff timestamp or trailing tab)
shortcuts.what: The whole rest of the line, timestamp included, is taken as the path. It doesn't equal "ledger/sheet.ts", so the header isn't mapped, and "ledger/sheet.ts\t2024-01-01 00:00:00" is reported as unmapped.

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content (context, removed, added lines) is mapped word by word through identifier entries; only file headers are path-mapped
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; a hunk after "@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@" containing the removed line "--- a/Sheet" (content "-- a/Sheet") or the added line "+++ b/Sheet" (content "++ b/Sheet")
shortcuts.what: There is no hunk tracking. Lines are classified by prefix alone, so a hunk content line starting with "--- a/" or "+++ b/" is treated as a file header. "Sheet" goes through path mapping instead of identifier mapping, so it stays "Sheet" instead of becoming "Invoice", and "Sheet" is wrongly reported as an unmapped path

shortcuts.rule: Every whole-word public identifier name in hunk content is replaced
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "$real" public "$pub" (or any public name containing regex metacharacters such as "$", "." or "("), hunk line "+$pub();"
shortcuts.what: Public names go into the RegExp without escaping. "$" is read as an anchor, so the name never matches and the line stays unchanged. Names with "." also match other text, and names with "(" make the RegExp throw

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content (context, removed, added lines) is mapped word by word
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; inside a hunk, a removed line whose text is "-- Sheet total" (diff line "--- Sheet total") or an added line "++ Sheet" (diff line "+++ Sheet")
shortcuts.what: With no hunk tracking, any line starting with "--- " or "+++ " is treated as a file header: without an a/ or b/ prefix it is returned unchanged, so "Sheet" is never mapped. A removed line "--- a/Sheet" is path-mapped instead, and the path gets reported as unmapped

shortcuts.rule: File header paths are mapped and unmapped paths are reported
shortcuts.input: A diff touching "docs/read me.md" (a path with a space): "diff --git a/docs/read me.md b/docs/read me.md", "--- a/docs/read me.md", "+++ b/docs/read me.md"
shortcuts.what: The header regexes use \S+ for the path. The diff --git line does not match at all and goes through identifier replacement. The ---/+++ lines treat "docs/read" as the path, so "docs/read" is reported as unmapped instead of "docs/read me.md". A path entry covering the full path would be looked up with a truncated path

shortcuts.rule: Identifier entries replace whole words, in one pass
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "$invoice" public "$sheet" and hunk line "+x = $sheet;"
shortcuts.what: Public names are joined into a RegExp without escaping and wrapped in \b. "$" is a regex anchor and \b does not treat "$" as part of a word, so "$sheet" is never replaced. Names with other regex metacharacters match the wrong text, or make the RegExp constructor throw

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content (context, removed and added lines) is mapped word by word
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; inside a hunk, the removed line "--- Sheet totals" (the removed text is "-- Sheet totals") next to the added line "+-- Sheet sums"
shortcuts.what: Lines are classified by prefix only, with no hunk tracking. Any line starting with "--- " or "+++ " counts as a file header and is skipped by identifier mapping, so the output keeps "--- Sheet totals" while the added line becomes "+-- Invoice sums". If such a line looks like "--- a/<path>" or "+++ b/<path>", it is path-mapped as a header instead, and the path may be reported as unmapped.

shortcuts.rule: Removed and added hunk lines are mapped word by word
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; a hunk (after "@@ -1 +1 @@") containing the removed line "--- Sheet" and the added line "+++ Sheet" (e.g. SQL comments "-- Sheet" / "++ Sheet")
shortcuts.what: The diff is processed line by line with no notion of being inside a hunk, so any line starting with "--- " or "+++ " is treated as a file header: these lines are returned unchanged instead of becoming "--- Invoice" / "+++ Invoice". Hunk lines such as "--- a/Sheet" are likewise path-mapped (and reported as unmapped) instead of identifier-mapped.

shortcuts.rule: whole-word public names in removed and added hunk lines are mapped
shortcuts.input: identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; a hunk whose removed line is "--- uses Sheet" (content "-- uses Sheet", e.g. an SQL comment) or whose added line is "+++ Sheet"
shortcuts.what: the code classifies each line by prefix only and does not track whether it is inside a hunk, so these lines match the bare "--- "/"+++ " header check and are returned unchanged, leaving "Sheet" unmapped

shortcuts.rule: hunk content is mapped word by word; only file headers have their paths mapped and reported as unmapped
shortcuts.input: a hunk with removed line "--- a/docs/notes.md" (content "-- a/docs/notes.md") and no path entry covering docs/notes.md
shortcuts.what: treats the hunk line as a "--- a/" file header: path-maps it, skips identifier mapping, and wrongly reports "docs/notes.md" as unmapped

shortcuts.rule: Every public path in the file header lines is mapped
shortcuts.input: Path entry real "billing" public "ledger"; the diff header "diff --git a/ledger/my file.ts b/ledger/my file.ts" (a path containing a space)
shortcuts.what: The diff --git regex accepts only paths with no whitespace (\S+), so that line falls through and is left as "ledger/my file.ts", while the ---/+++ lines become "billing/my file.ts". The path is not reported as unmapped either.

shortcuts.rule: Hunk content is mapped word by word, and lines that hold no public name are unchanged
shortcuts.input: Identifier entry real "Invoice" public "Sheet"; inside a hunk, a removed line whose content is "-- a/Sheet" (the diff line "--- a/Sheet")
shortcuts.what: The code does not track whether a line is inside a hunk, so it parses this line as a file header. "Sheet" stays unmapped in the output, and "Sheet" is reported as an unmapped path. An added line "++ b/..." gets the same treatment, and with a matching path entry such hunk lines are path-rewritten.
